To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
massage does not improve hamstring function, but does reduce the intensity of muscle soreness.
massage administered 2 h postexercise did not improve hamstring ROM and peak torque but did reduce the subjective intensity of soreness at 48 h.
massage administered 2 h following exercise-induced muscle injury did not reduce muscle soreness, but did reduce the perceived intensity of soreness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of massage on delayed-onset muscle soreness ( DOMS ) induced by a single bout of eccentric exercise.
the physiological and psychological benefits of massage on DOMS.
the effects of massage administered 2 hours post exercise-induced muscle soreness (delayed onset muscle soreness, DOMS) on muscle function and soreness intensity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
massage is not an effective intervention for reducing the symptoms of DOMS.
massage does not appear to be effective in reducing the symptoms of delayed onset muscle sorenes.
massage is effective in reducing the intensity of muscle soreness 48 hours after muscle insult.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
massage is an effective intervention in reducing the intensity of sorensess, but it has no effect on other physiological parameters.
massage is an effective treatment for reducing the intensity of sore muscles.
massage may be an effective method to reduce the intensity of delayed onset muscle sorensess.
The main takeaway from our work is that
massage may not be an effective treatment for DOMS but may help to reduce soreness 48-72 h after exercise.
the effects of massage on soreness are likely to be delayed and that massage may be most effective if administered after muscle injury has occurred.
massage is a safe and effective intervention for the management of DOMS.
